title: screenpipe
one_line_problem: Knowledge workers' computer activity is invisible to the AI agents that are meant to help with that work.
short_description: screenpipe records a user's computer work locally and turns it into searchable context that agents can use. The README positions it for companies that want to map workflows and find work worth automating.

title: Rowboat
one_line_problem: Teams running several AI agents have no shared workspace where agents and people hand off work and see what each step did.
short_description: Rowboat connects agents the team already runs, such as Claude Code, Hermes or OpenClaw, into one workspace. Agents and people share chat, whiteboards, docs and task lists, and every step stays visible.

title: Parlant
one_line_problem: Customer-facing AI agents are hard to configure and behave unpredictably in live conversations.
short_description: Parlant is a framework for building conversational customer-service agents. The README says it is driven from a coding agent such as Claude Code, and it includes a session dashboard, shown in the README screenshot.

title: DocsGPT
one_line_problem: Teams want AI answers grounded in their own documents, with sources, and the data should stay in their own environment.
short_description: DocsGPT turns documents, websites and connected apps into AI agents that answer with sources. Agents can be embedded as a chat widget, called through an OpenAI-compatible API, or exposed as an MCP server, with cloud or local models.

title: Labelme
one_line_problem: Training vision models needs hand-labelled images, and labelling tools are often heavy or hard to install.
short_description: Labelme is a Python and Qt desktop tool for drawing shapes on images to create labels. The README shows examples for bounding boxes, classification, and instance and semantic segmentation, and points to a standalone app on labelme.io.

title: Rerun
one_line_problem: Robotics and vision engineers log multimodal data from many sources and need to inspect it together over time.
short_description: Rerun ingests multi-rate data such as images, point clouds, transforms and time series from robot logs, simulation and video. It stores the data in columnar form and provides a viewer, which the README also offers in the browser.

title: pytorch-grad-cam
one_line_problem: Deep vision models give predictions with no visible reason, which makes diagnosing errors and building trust hard.
short_description: pytorch-grad-cam is a pip-installable package of class-activation-map methods that highlight the image regions driving a PyTorch model's prediction. The README shows examples for detection and segmentation as well as classification.

title: Instant NGP
one_line_problem: Neural radiance fields were too slow to train and render for interactive use.
short_description: Instant NGP implements neural graphics primitives (NeRF, signed distance functions, neural images and volumes) using a multiresolution hash encoding. The README includes a GUI testbed and a project-page video.
result: README claim, not measured here: a NeRF of a fox can be trained in under 5 seconds.

title: CARLA
one_line_problem: Autonomous-driving systems need safe, repeatable test environments before they run on real roads.
short_description: CARLA is an open-source simulator for autonomous-driving research. It ships open urban layouts, buildings and vehicles, and supports flexible sensor suites and environmental conditions.

title: OpenCat Quadruped Robot
one_line_problem: Building a walking quadruped robot means writing gait, servo and sensor code from scratch.
short_description: OpenCat is an open-source Arduino and Raspberry Pi framework for quadruped robots. It handles gait coordination, servo control and IMU integration, and the README notes that it covers the legacy NyBoard platform.

title: Sesame Robot
one_line_problem: Makers want an accessible walking robot with expressive movement, on an ESP32 platform, without a steep learning curve.
short_description: Sesame is an open-source ESP32 walking-robot project with an emphasis on expression and movement. The repo covers firmware and a companion app, and the README aims it at makers of all skill levels.

title: JPL Open Source Rover
one_line_problem: Students and makers have no open, affordable six-wheel rover platform based on a real planetary-rover design.
short_description: A scaled-down, build-it-yourself six-wheel rover based on the design JPL uses for Mars exploration, built from consumer off-the-shelf parts. The repository includes the Onshape CAD designs and documentation.

title: evcc
one_line_problem: Households with EV chargers and solar panels want to coordinate charging and energy use locally, without cloud services.
short_description: evcc lets a household steer its electric-car charging, and other home energy use, from software it runs itself. The README states the aim as keeping that coordination local, so no cloud service is needed.

title: PiKVM
one_line_problem: Remote management of a machine fails when its operating system is unhealthy, because most remote tools need the OS running.
short_description: PiKVM is a DIY IP-KVM built on a Raspberry Pi. It gives network access to a machine's keyboard, video and mouse, and the README describes it as working regardless of the health of the operating system. A web UI screenshot is included.

title: OpenMower
one_line_problem: Most robotic lawn mowers move in random patterns, which the project considers inefficient.
short_description: OpenMower is an open-source DIY robotic lawn mower. Its firmware, software and hardware designs live in several linked repositories, and this repo is the entry point, with openmower.de as the start page.

title: Server Box
one_line_problem: Checking and managing servers from a phone usually means juggling several SSH clients and monitoring tools.
short_description: Server Box is a Flutter and Rust app that shows status charts for Linux, Unix and Windows servers and provides tools to manage them. It connects over SSH, through a jump host, or through an HTTP monitor agent, and includes a terminal.

title: Anx Reader
one_line_problem: E-book readers tend to be either plain or bloated, and few handle many book formats with AI help in one modern app.
short_description: Anx Reader is a cross-platform e-book reader for EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, TXT and PDF, with AI features and a modern interface. The README includes a feature table and screenshots for phone and wide layouts.

title: GSY GitHub App
one_line_problem: Power users want a richer and more pleasant GitHub client than the official app for managing their own account.
short_description: A cross-platform open-source GitHub client built with Flutter, aimed at day-to-day management of a personal GitHub account. The English README lists sibling implementations in Weex, React Native and native Android Kotlin.

title: bottom
one_line_problem: Terminal users want one view of CPU, memory, network and processes without installing several monitoring tools.
short_description: bottom is a cross-platform terminal system monitor. It draws CPU, RAM and swap usage as graphs over time, with per-core CPU views, and the README documents its widgets and install paths.

title: gh-dash
one_line_problem: Keeping up with GitHub pull requests and issues means constantly switching between browser tabs and filters.
short_description: gh-dash is a rich terminal UI for GitHub. The README pitches it as a way to stay on top of GitHub work without breaking your flow, and it has a demo overview GIF.

title: VHS
one_line_problem: Demonstrating or regression-testing command-line tools means recording terminal sessions by hand, which cannot be reproduced.
short_description: VHS writes terminal GIFs from plain-text tape scripts, so CLI demos and integration checks can be regenerated from code. The README shows the tape syntax with rendered example GIFs.

title: Documenso
one_line_problem: Every e-signature sent through a third-party tool adds a provider the signer has to trust.
short_description: Documenso is an open-source document-signing platform, positioned as an alternative to DocuSign. It can be self-hosted or used through documenso.com, and the README includes a product video.

title: DocuSeal
one_line_problem: Filling and signing PDF forms online usually needs a paid, closed service.
short_description: DocuSeal is an open-source platform for creating PDF forms, collecting signatures and filling documents online on any device. The README highlights a WYSIWYG form-field builder.

title: Maxun
one_line_problem: Turning website content into structured data usually means writing scrapers that break whenever the page changes.
short_description: Maxun is an open-source web data platform for scraping, crawling, monitoring and AI-assisted extraction. The README describes extracting structured data by emulating real user behaviour, and turning a site into a structured API.

title: Peach
one_line_problem: Personal video libraries lack organised metadata about the people and works in them, and collecting it by hand is tedious.
short_description: Peach is a local-first video metadata scraper and media manager. It organises people, works, follows and statistics, and the README links a live demo built on sample movie data.

title: Rybbit
one_line_problem: Site owners want web analytics such as sessions, pageviews and funnels, either as a hosted service or on their own servers.
short_description: Rybbit is an open-source web analytics platform. It covers sessions, unique users, pageviews, bounce rate and session duration, with customisable goals, retention, user-journey and funnel dashboards.

title: Perspective
one_line_problem: Analysts need interactive pivot tables and charts over large or streaming datasets without a heavy server-side stack.
short_description: Perspective is an open-source data grid, pivot table and charting component for large, real-time datasets. The README says its streaming query engine runs in the browser through WebAssembly, and it includes example dashboards.

title: ActivityWatch
one_line_problem: People want to see how they spend time on their computer without handing that data to a cloud service.
short_description: ActivityWatch is an open-source automated time tracker. Watchers record activity, and the data is stored on the user's own machine. The README states the goal of collecting personal activity data without compromising privacy.

title: Apache Superset
one_line_problem: Teams need a self-service BI tool to explore data and build charts and dashboards on top of many SQL databases.
short_description: Apache Superset is an enterprise-ready business-intelligence web application. It covers exploring data, building charts and dashboards, and querying databases in SQL Lab, and the README links user and admin guides.
